licences.notes: Words as printed in the Peters vocal score: conjugi (the chorus), gioja, Fiordiligi's “cresce, cresce” and Dorabella's single “cresce”, and the sisters' and officers' toasts as printed (“Tocca e bevi”, “Bevi e tocca”, each sung several times).

licences.source: Edition Peters vocal score (Edition Peters Nr. 4474, plate 11446, edited by Georg Schünemann), pages 316–325, bars 66–172 of No. 31
licences.author: Kurt Soldan (1891–1946), piano reduction
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the No. 31 Finale (671 bars) read in fourteen page ranges, sung lines and piano each by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the zoomed page by a judge, a separate sweep for dynamics and other marks, then checked bar by bar by eight fresh proofreaders (pages 311–324 clean). The German singing translation is left out. All the singers of this section have a staff throughout, with rests where the print leaves a staff out; singers who do not sing in this section are left out. The chorus (sopranos, altos, tenors and basses; servants and musicians) has a staff for each part and is heard with the piano; it has no role here. Where the print gives the basses no words, they sing the tenors' words. Cut from the one-file finale at bars 66–172: from the Andante (E♭ major, alla breve) to the bar with the fermata before the Larghetto. The cut Peters marks (“vi-” in bar 2 to “-de” in bar 60) is not made. In bar 87 a slur printed between the two voices of the right hand is not encoded. Playback tempo ♩ = 106 (a half note = 53) from René Jacobs's recording (harmonia mundi), 4:03.
